title: Rust indexing TypeScript replacement readiness
description: Decision map for whether rust-indexing can fully replace TypeScript indexing.

decisions.q: Can Rust cover all currently supported product languages?
decisions.note: Rust core SourceLanguage currently covers JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, MTS, CTS, and Go; README-supported languages include Python, Java, C#, PHP, Ruby, C/C++, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Dart, Svelte, Vue, Liquid, Pascal/Delphi, Lua, and Luau.

decisions.q: Can Rust replace TS semantic behavior for JS/TS-owned files now?
decisions.answer: Not fully; it is much closer, but still bounded.
decisions.note: Recent work completed TypeScript moduleResolution semantic frontier slices, including JSON resolveJsonModule file-level edges. However research/no-go boundaries remain for typesVersions, symlink identity, package-manager edge cases, type graph semantics, and broader declaration/runtime exactness.

decisions.q: Should the product remove TypeScript indexing now?
decisions.answer: No; keep TypeScript as fallback and explicit escape hatch.
decisions.note: PRD and README define rust-hybrid as default: Rust-owned files first, TypeScript fallback for unsupported languages and per-file Rust gaps, plus explicit zcodegraph index --engine typescript troubleshooting path.

decisions.q: Can rust-indexing fully replace ts-indexing now?
decisions.answer: No. It can be the default primary path through rust-hybrid, but not a complete replacement.
decisions.note: Replacement would require Rust-owned coverage for the full supported language matrix, closing remaining JS/TS semantic frontiers or explicitly productizing their no-go boundaries, and release evidence showing no sufficiency regression without TS fallback.

1-5.label: Reduce TypeScript fallback surface by migrating Rust-owned languages

decisions.q: What replaces the pure Rust replacement goal?
decisions.answer: Reduce TypeScript fallback surface area incrementally.
decisions.note: Keep rust-hybrid as the product contract. Move already-supported product languages into Rust-owned indexing one by one when the bounded extraction, fallback diagnostics, and sufficiency evidence are credible.

1-5-1.label: Rust-owned Python indexing v1

decisions.q: Which supported language should be migrated next into Rust-owned indexing?
decisions.note: Python is already product-supported through the TypeScript extractor and framework resolvers, but Rust core SourceLanguage currently owns only JS/JSX/TS/TSX/MTS/CTS/Go. This is a fallback-surface reduction, not a new user-visible language claim.

1-5-1.notes: Deferred. Python is already product-supported through TypeScript fallback, but Rust-owned Python migration expands the language set and should be handled as a separate target after the current Rust-owned JS/TS/Go dependency cleanup.

1-5-2.label: Eliminate TypeScript indexing dependency for current Rust-owned languages

decisions.q: What should be optimized before adding Python as another Rust-owned language?
decisions.answer: Remove same-language TypeScript indexing dependency for current Rust-owned languages as much as possible.
decisions.note: Scope is JS, JSX, TS, TSX, MTS, CTS, and Go. Keep TypeScript fallback for non-Rust-owned product languages and explicit --engine typescript, but stop relying on TS indexer to recover ordinary Rust-owned parse/extraction gaps unless explicitly classified as a remaining blocker.

decisions.q: What should happen when a Rust-owned JS/TS/Go file has a parse or extraction gap?
decisions.answer: Default no same-language TypeScript fallback; surface degraded/fail-closed diagnostics instead.
decisions.note: Current users are limited, so release-risk minimization is less important than eliminating the architectural trap of maintaining Rust and TypeScript indexers as equivalent implementations for the same Rust-owned languages. Non-Rust-owned product languages may still use TypeScript fallback.

1-5-2.notes: Completed by issues #475-#478. Implementation plan: docs/plans/2026-06-23-remove-same-language-typescript-fallback-for-rust-owned-languages.md. Closeout evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-06-23-remove-same-language-typescript-fallback-closeout.md. Rust-owned JS/JSX/TS/TSX/MTS/CTS/Go gaps no longer append same-language TypeScript fallback; non-Rust-owned language fallback and explicit --engine typescript remain.
